Text as polygon outlines

Source: R/text.R
lari_text_outline.Rd

Shape a string with 'textshaping' and flatten each glyph outline with 'systemfonts', returning the closed rings of every glyph. Letters with counters (A, B, O, ...) come back as an outer ring and one or more hole rings; lari_glyphs() meshes them.

Usage

lari_text_outline(text, em = 1, tolerance = 0.002, ..., res = 1000)

Arguments

text

a character string (newlines start new lines)

em

the size of one em (the font size) in output units

tolerance

the maximum distance between the flattened outline and the curves of the font, in output units

...

passed to textshaping::shape_text(), e.g. family, weight, italic, path (a font file), lineheight, align, tracking

res

the internal shaping size (larger keeps more precision)

Value

a data frame with x, y, glyph (the glyph's position in the shaped string), ring (the outline contour within the glyph), and char (the glyph's character, empty when one character does not map to one glyph). Rings are not closed (the first vertex is not repeated) and their orientation is whatever the font uses.

Details

Coordinates are in ems: with the default em = 1 one unit is one em, so max_area and tolerance read the same whatever the font. Shaping is done at res and scaled down, so the glyph outlines keep full precision. Font fallback is respected (each glyph is read from the font file textshaping chose for it).

See also

lari_glyphs(), lari_text()

Examples

o <- lari_text_outline("B")
table(o$ring)
#> 
#>  1  2  3 
#> 35 35 67
